title: Grove keeps a fully scaffolded but Inactive Executor Transformation Primitive despite being a Prime Agent
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.1.2.3.1.1.1 declares flatly that "Grove is a Prime Agent," and the Prime Transformation Primitive's Global Activation Status (A.6.1.1.2.2.1.2.1.1) reads `Completed`. Yet A.6.1.1.2.2.1.3 still carries a complete Executor Transformation Primitive subtree — Hub Document, all four status directories, Hub Data Repository with Failed and Suspended subtrees — with Global Activation Status (A.6.1.1.2.2.1.3.1.1) reading `Inactive`.

The observation is about how the Atlas is built rather than about Grove specifically: **Primitive slots are instantiated uniformly, and non-applicability is expressed as a status value rather than as absence**. An unused capability is present-and-off, not missing.

This has a real benefit. Every Agent Artifact has the same shape at the same addresses, so cross-Agent comparison and tooling work by position, and activating a dormant capability is a status change rather than a structural amendment.

It also explains the Atlas's low signal density. A large fraction of any Agent Artifact consists of correctly-formed empty containers, which is why extracting claims from these documents means distinguishing `Inactive` scaffolding from live specification.
description: Its Prime Transformation Primitive is Completed while the Executor path stays Inactive with empty directories — the Atlas instantiates every Primitive slot for every Agent, used or not.
